tips.title: How to direct a longer Seedance 2.5 scene
items: Write one clear story arc with a beginning, transition and ending.
Assign one camera move to each timed beat instead of stacking directions.
Describe visible causes and reactions to keep physical motion readable.
Keep dialogue brief and pair each line with a specific action or expression.

tabs.label: Concept
tabs.title: Define the scene arc
tabs.description: Establish who is present, what changes and where the scene must end.
tabs.copy:
Subject and setting:
[Who appears, where they are, and the defining visual details]

Story change:
[What happens from the opening moment to the final beat]

Ending frame:
[The final action, expression or composition]

Visual language:
[Lighting, palette, texture and lens character]

tabs.label: Timeline
tabs.title: Direct timed story beats
tabs.description: Map actions and camera movement across the full duration.
tabs.copy:
0-6 seconds:
[Opening composition + first action + camera move]

6-14 seconds:
[Development beat + reaction + camera transition]

14-22 seconds:
[Main reveal or performance beat + framing]

22-30 seconds:
[Resolution + final camera position]

Audio direction:
[Ambience, brief dialogue and action-linked sound cues]

tabs.label: Constraints
tabs.title: Protect continuity and clarity
tabs.description: State the elements that cannot drift while the scene develops.
tabs.copy:
Continuity anchors:
[Wardrobe, props, location, lighting and screen direction]

Physical rules:
[Contact, weight, speed and environmental reactions]

Performance rules:
[Eye lines, gestures, facial expression and dialogue timing]

Avoid:
[Unwanted cuts, duplicate subjects, abrupt camera changes and visual artifacts]

tabNotes.body: Concept sets one readable narrative change for the whole scene.
Timeline assigns one action and one camera move to each beat.
Constraints repeat only the details that must remain stable.

globalPrinciples: Describe a complete scene arc before adding shot-level detail.
Use time ranges to sequence actions instead of requesting everything at once.
Keep camera language deliberate and physically compatible with the scene.
Tie gestures, expressions and brief dialogue to visible story beats.
engineWhy: Longer scene planning gives setup, development and payoff enough room to read.
Timed direction makes camera movement and performance easier to evaluate beat by beat.
Explicit physical rules help preserve believable motion and reactions across the sequence.

demo.title: Seedance 2.5 timeline demonstration
demo.prompt: A grounded city sequence unfolds through clear timed beats. Begin with a wide establishing move, follow one readable human action, transition to a closer performance moment, then settle on a composed ending frame. Keep wardrobe, lighting, direction of movement and environmental reactions consistent throughout.
notes: Use the visible action and camera transition to check whether each timed beat remains readable.
The audio label matches the selected render.
